page: Microsoft Azure D32ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadsv7 server family. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The configuration provides 32 virtual CPUs across 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Additionally, the instance features 1890 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, while lacking any dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate highly competitive single-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression single-threaded tests all rank in the top tier (top 10%). Multi-threaded performance is also robust, with the passmark CPU score, extended instructions, and encryption tests placing in the strong top 25% bracket. However, multi-core stress-ng performance and database operations fall into the average middle 50% category. Memory bandwidth and Redis SET operations also demonstrate average performance characteristics.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D32ads_v7 offers a balanced resource density of compute, memory, and high-speed local storage. The inclusion of a fast 1890 GB NVMe SSD provides strong storage-to-compute value without requiring external storage attachments for high-throughput local operations. This hardware profile is well-suited for general-purpose enterprise workloads, web serving, single-threaded data compression tasks, and moderate database operations. It is also capable of handling small-scale LLM inference tasks, where it achieves top-tier text generation speeds for small models.
